start.text: The next cresset up the road stands just past the Unmoored, out in the fog. Somebody has put it out on purpose: the coals raked out onto the cairn and trodden into the cinder, the basket packed to the rim with wet black grit, and a flat stone set on top like a lid on a pot.
Three days to get it cold, Ness said.
Past it the road goes on up towards the crown, and forgets.
The ember stirs in your hand at the sight of it. Behind you, in the fog, somebody stands up.
